svg.title: Shipped, moving, and open: what MCP does and does not yet answer
svg.desc: Three columns of identical width. The first, headed Shipped on a green band and ticked three times, lists the 2026-07-28 core, described as three primitives, two transports and one discovery method and marked finished; io.modelcontextprotocol/ui, which is MCP Apps, stable at 2026-01-26 with eleven hosts on the client matrix; and the enterprise-managed authorization extension, stable with one host on the matrix. A note adds that stable here means a dated or stable specification directory. The second column, headed Moving on an amber band and marked with clock faces, lists the tasks extension, whose SEP is final but whose specification is still at draft, whose repository describes itself as experimental and which is absent from the client matrix; the OAuth client-credentials extension, at draft with no client listed as supporting it; and seven experimental repositories, interceptors, variants, skills, grouping, tool-annotations, triggers-events and server-card, with a note that each repository expresses stability differently. The third column, headed Open on a grey band and marked with crosses, lists three things with no accepted proposal at all: tool-definition pinning, because nothing lets a client detect that an approved tool changed; identity, because authorization exists but portable end-user identity does not; and agent to agent, because MCP describes one host and many servers and no agent calling another agent. A band across the foot draws the five steps of the Extensions Track, propose, implement, review, publish and adopt, with implement outlined in terracotta because at least one reference implementation in an official SDK is required before the proposal can be reviewed, not before it is accepted but before it is read. Two closing lines note that adoption is everyone else's decision rather than the author's, and that promotion into core is optional and needs its own Standards Track proposal, because plenty of extensions should stay extensions forever.
svg.text: The third column is the honest answer to "is MCP finished?"
Stable. One host on the matrix.
Stable = a dated or stable/ spec directory.
SEP Final, spec still at draft.
No accepted proposal for any of the three.
At least one reference implementation in an official SDK is REQUIRED before the SEP can be reviewed. Not before it is accepted: before it is read.
Promotion into core is optional and needs its own Standards Track SEP. Plenty of extensions should stay extensions forever.
